$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-5y(t),\end{aligned}\,[\begin{aligned}x(0) \\ y(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the solution to the initial value problem above.

*Hint: ${e}^{At}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-5t} & t{e}^{-5t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-5t}\end{aligned}],$ where $A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$*

Writing our system in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/0bbfb7f1e06945c024621e567e852daa3262e761f537c915152361d6b93e3f68.svg)
where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/ae94bee2846b9b53317233c4013d1b42ddd07303854d4b0fbf7daf3af46a02d7.svg) So, the matrix of the system is ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/aafe76b34e120360b2af30f6d2a0d1c9ebab98302c2bf002baab7a0c8ab1ed44.svg)

Given the system $\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix, the solution of the initial value problem can be written as

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi_0(t) \, \mathbf{x}(0),
$$

where $\Phi_0(t) = e^{At}$ is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and $\mathbf{x}(0)$ is the initial condition vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix $\Phi_0(t)$ of the system is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14150255/assets/c412649960553152d3a43e92c4523e944326013a9e1d51e198ef5911e5a7c9b4.svg)

Therefore, the solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{At}\,x(0) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
